opportunities.title: Binance Knew for 8 Weeks: The Anatomy of a Breach Nobody Wanted to See
opportunities.why_now: SEAL's report that attackers sat inside Binance for eight weeks before a $6.3B exploit is the kind of detail that turns a hack story into an indictment of monitoring culture.
opportunities.angle: Security autopsy — timeline breakdown of the 8-week dwell time, what alerts should have fired, and why 'time to detect' is the metric exchanges never publish

opportunities.title: Chainalysis Got Hacked. The Company That Tracks Hackers.
opportunities.why_now: Password hashes and live tokens exposed at a firm whose entire business is crypto forensics is the irony that writes itself and deserves a sharp, specific breakdown.
opportunities.angle: Short, pointed blog + X thread on the credibility paradox — if the trackers can't secure their own creds, what exactly are they selling?

opportunities.title: Gnosis Pay Breach: When Your Card, Your Wallet, and Your Name Live on the Same Server
opportunities.why_now: Gnosis Pay just proved that crypto-card convergence means a single breach now leaks both TradFi payment data and on-chain wallet identity in one shot.
opportunities.angle: Explainer on the new attack surface created by crypto debit cards — map what data actually got exposed and what it enables (phishing, SIM-swap targeting, doxxing)

opportunities.title: Every Exchange Suddenly Has Great Cold Storage Ratios. Funny Timing.
opportunities.why_now: Exchanges rushing to publicize cold-wallet percentages right after the Binance hack is a textbook reactive-PR pattern worth calling out before it's forgotten.
opportunities.angle: Skeptical take-down — compare pre- and post-hack disclosures, note which exchanges went quiet, and explain why a 'ratio' without proof-of-reserves is just a number

opportunities.title: A Fake Teams Invite Took Down API Keys at Binance and Deribit — That's the Whole Playbook Now
opportunities.why_now: SignalPlus getting compromised via a fake Teams meeting invite shows the entry point for the next big hack is rarely a smart-contract bug — it's a calendar invite.
opportunities.angle: Tactical breakdown of the social-engineering vector for X/thread format, framed as 'this is how it actually starts' for traders and treasury teams using third-party tools/APIs
